status_summary: No bill or Treasury statement to move the Coast Guard or ATF to Treasury, and no congressional examination of the idea, was found; the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025 (H.R. 4275), which passed the House 399-12 on 2025-07-23 and was referred to the Senate Commerce Committee the same day, shows no transfer action in its bill status, and a Senate bill on Coast Guard leadership (S. 1190) keeps the Coast Guard in Homeland Security. The Justice Department's FY2026 request proposed folding ATF into the Drug Enforcement Administration, a move within Justice rather than to Treasury, and a House subcommittee bill advanced 2025-07-15 would bar funds for shifting ATF functions, according to a news report; the merger was not carried out. The enacted appropriations law (Public Law 119-74, from H.R. 6938, enacted 2026-01-23) funds ATF at 1,585,000,000 dollars as a separate bureau and bars use of funds made available by that or any other Act to transfer ATF's functions, missions or activities to other agencies or Departments, a fiscal year 2026 condition that does not address the Coast Guard.

timeline.event: House Appropriations CJS subcommittee advanced the FY2026 bill that, per a news report, bars funds to move ATF responsibilities to other agencies and blocks the proposed ATF and DEA merger.

Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938, fiscal year 2026 Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment appropriations) is enacted. Its enrolled text appropriates 1,585,000,000 dollars for ATF salaries and expenses as a separate bureau, with a proviso barring use of funds made available by that or any other Act to transfer ATF's functions, missions or activities to other agencies or Departments.

title: Examine returning the Coast Guard and ATF to Treasury
uncertainties: No bill, order or law moving the Coast Guard or ATF to Treasury was found. The Justice Department's FY2026 request to fold ATF into DEA, read through news summaries, was a move within Justice and was not carried out. DHS pages are blocked. The Unified Agenda rule lists on reginfo.gov for Treasury, Homeland Security and Justice (headed 'Agency Rule List - 2026') list no transfer; a transfer needs legislation, so the agenda is a weak test. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19. Update 2026-10-22: the enrolled text of Public Law 119-74 was opened on govinfo.gov: the ATF salaries and expenses appropriation of 1,585,000,000 dollars carries a proviso barring use of funds made available by that or any other Act to transfer ATF's functions, missions or activities to other agencies or Departments; the proviso does not name DEA or Treasury. The opened text was cut short before the general provisions, so an external retrieval's report of a separate bar on moving the ATF canine training center (section 543) and of no Coast Guard text in the law was not confirmed. The bar is part of a fiscal year 2026 act; Public Law 119-103 (approved 2026-09-02, opened on govinfo.gov) section 101 continues funding under the conditions of the fiscal year 2026 Acts, listing division A of Public Law 119-74 with exceptions for sections 521(c)(2) and 544 only, and section 106 ends that availability no later than 2026-12-11; that the ATF bar continues to apply under it is an inference. The defense authorization law (Public Law 119-60) was read only through its table of contents on govinfo.gov, which lists section 7207, Coast Guard access to a Department of the Treasury fund, in Division G; an external retrieval reports that the section concerns a Treasury forfeiture fund (31 U.S.C. 9705), that Division G is the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, and that the law contains no transfer of the Coast Guard to Treasury; that reading was not confirmed. GovInfo bill status records were opened for four bills. H.R. 6938 (Rep. Tom Cole, introduced 2026-01-06) passed the House 397-28 on 2026-01-08 and the Senate 82-15 on 2026-01-15 and became Public Law 119-74 on 2026-01-23; its actions do not mention ATF, the Coast Guard or Treasury. H.R. 5342 (House CJS bill, Rep. Harold Rogers) and S. 2354 (Senate CJS bill, Sen. Jerry Moran) show committee reports and calendar placement (2025-09-12 and 2025-07-17) and no later action; status records carry no bill text, so funding-bar language reported for those two bills was not confirmed. H.R. 4275 (Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025, Rep. Sam Graves, four cosponsors) passed the House 399-12 on 2025-07-23 and was referred to the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee the same day with no later action; its status record shows no transfer action, though its text was not read. An external retrieval ran 17 searches on 2026-10-22 and reported no bill, appropriations provision or executive action moving the Coast Guard or ATF to Treasury; it also reported a Coast Guard Treasury forfeiture fund provision in H.R. 4275 (section 222) that does not transfer the service, a 2025-03-25 Justice Department reorganization memo and a 2025-06-13 budget summary proposing to fold ATF into DEA, and press reporting of 2026-01-17 that the plan was abandoned. Those items were not opened and no formal withdrawal document was located. ATF and DEA merger items are moves within Justice, not to Treasury, and are related context rather than stage events.
